Windows are a common heat loss point for building in cold climates, both through the glass and around the frame. 3.9 Ventilation The Moore Street apartment building currently has no central ventilation system. Ventilation is exhaust-only and consists of bath fans and range hoods in each of the 20 units. The bath fans are manually switch-operated with a humidistat back-up. The range hoods are operated by a manual on/off switch. This exhaust-only ventilation relies on passive air entry through small openings and air leakage pathways around windows and doors for fresh air. The building has one heat recovery ventilator (HRV) (see Figure 9), which provides ventilation to two storage closets when it is operational. The HRV was not operating at the time of the survey. 12 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 9. The building has one HRV in a storage closet, which is not operational. There are many things to consider when choosing a ventilation system: • Energy efficiency upgrades—such as new windows, adding insulation, and air sealing— will result in the building being more airtight. While this will help to reduce energy bill costs and increase comfort, it will also reduce the building’s ability to bring in outside air when exhaust ventilation is operating. A balanced ventilation system that can bring in fresh air when it exhausts stale air becomes necessary. Continuing to rely on exhaust only ventilation as the building is upgraded will likely not be able to maintain a healthy amount of fresh air. • It is likely not feasible to retrofit a whole building ventilation system. While ducting for the first floor could run through the crawlspace, there is not an obvious place to run ducting that is not visible for units on the upper floor. • Unit balanced ventilation options do exist. HRVs can be installed in closets and exhaust stale air and bring in fresh air to a single apartment unit. In a cold climate such as Fairbanks, using an HRV to recapture heat that would otherwise leave the building with stale air is beneficial as opposed to ventilation options that exhaust heated air and bring in untempered cold air. These units have variable programming options to operate a portion of each hour depending on occupancy. They can also have a filter box in line with the air intake to install higher minimum efficiency reporting value filters, which can help prevent particulate matter pollution from wildfires or exhaust from entering the building. 3.10 Energy Efficiency Considerations Energy efficiency upgrades for Moore Street Senior
